Kabc020027652022 
 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
 Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. 
 Dated This The 20th Day Of November 2024 
Present: Sri.Kumara.S (B.A., Ll.B)
 Vii Addl. Scj and Acjm,
 Member, Mact-3, Bengaluru.

 S/o Muniyappa,
 Aged about 30 years,

 Bangalore East,

Respondents : 01. Sri.Sangamesh,
 No.263/P1, Khane Road,
 Kalkere,
 Horamavu Post,
 (Scch-3) 2 M.V.C.No.608/2022
 Behind Hp Petrol Bunk,
 Bangalore - 560 043.
 (R.C. Owner of Ashok Leyland Tempo

 (By Sri.Gururaj Salur, Advocate)
 *******
 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 
02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
That on 09.11.2021 at about 04.15 p.m, the petitioner was riding the Bike bearing No.
KA-53-HA-4725 along with pillion rider by name (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.608/2022 Munivenkatappa @ Appayanna, on the extreme left side of Manduru - Gunduru Road, when he reached near BMTC Depot Turning Cross, Bidarahalli Hobli,
Bengaluru, at that time suddenly the driver of Ashok Leyland Tempo bearing No.KA-53-AA-0761 came from opposite direction i.e., from Mandur side, in rash and negligent manner and came to his extreme right i.e., wrong side and dashed against the petitioners' Bike and caused the accident, due to which the petitioner fell down along with the Bike and sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to East Point hospital, Bengaluru, wherein admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges and prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years and was doing wood cutter labour work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner till today cannot attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning capacity and put to great financial hardship. The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Ashok Leyland Tempo and in this regard the Avalahalli Police have registered a case against the driver of the said (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.608/2022 offending Ashok Leyland Tempo. The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner of the said offending vehicle and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner together with interest and costs. 
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, he was placed exparte. 
04. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits issuance of the policy to the Ashok Leyland Tempo bearing No.KA-53-AA-0761 and the liability of this respondent is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy. It is further denied age, avocation, income of the petitioner, manner of accident and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petitioner was not wearing safety headgear at the time of alleged accident and Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/
2 the driver of the tempo was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.608/2022 accident, which is contravention of the policy conditions and the said tempo was not having valid fitness certificate at the time of accident and there is delay in lodging the complaint and the compensation claimed is highly excessive and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01. Whether the petitioner prove that when he was riding the Bike bearing No.
KA-53-HA-4725 he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 09.11.2021 at about 04.15 p.m, on Manduru - Gunduru Road, near B.M.T.C Depot Turning Cross, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Ashok Leyland Tempo bearing registration No.KA-53-AA-0761 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1and got examined doctor (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.608/2022 who treated the petitioner and assessed the disability as PW.2 and they have got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed petitioner side evidence. On behalf of the respondent No.2, the MRO and its Legal Manager got examined as RW.1 and 2 and through them got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and learned counsel for the petitioner has filed written arguments and perused the records. 
08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein. During the course of Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/
3 cross- examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he denied (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.608/2022 to the suggestion that he was riding the Motor Cycle by consuming alcohol and also denied to the suggestion that when he was riding the Motor Cycle one Lorry came and hit against him and denied to the suggestion that as the Tempo bearing No.KA-53-AA-0761 did not caused accident, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.
10. Further, PW.2 is doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief-examination evidence that the said petitioner has sustained communited fracture of proximal tibia and fibula right leg and he assessed permanent physical disability of 44% of right lower limb which is 22% of whole body and also stated that petitioner needs further treatment for malunion of tibia and implant removal and has produced OPD card and X-ray as per Ex.P.17 and 18. During the course of cross- examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that as per Ex.P.6 it is mentioned that history of RTA two wheeler v/s lorry and admits that in Ex.P.6 it is also mentioned as history of alcohol intake plus and admits that now the petitioner will walk without any support and the fractures are mal-united, there is no necessity of re-correction of surgery for mal-union and (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.608/2022 there is no shortening of right limb, the petitioner can do daily activities with some difficulties and the petitioner can do job by sitting and he assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and now the implants are ready for removal and now the petitioner is not under any treatment.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 on his behalf. Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Avalahalli Police, against the driver of offending Ashok Leyland Tempo bearing No.KA-53-AA-0761. Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint given against driver of offending Ashok Leyland Tempo for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner. Ex.P.3 is the copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending Ashok Layland Tempo for his rash and negligent driving and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner. But the Investigation Officer has not invoked the provisions of Sec.185 of IMV Act for drunk and drive and no evidence to show it is detected in a breath analyzer test that the driver/rider has in his blood alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.608/2022 blood. Ex.4 is copy of Spot Mahazar. Ex.P.5 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner which shows that he sustained grievous injuries. Ex.P.6 is copy of the Discharge summary of East Point hospital,
Bengaluru, which discloses that the petitioner was admitted from 09.11.2021 to 19.11.2021 as inpatient nearly for 10 days due to accidental injuries. Ex.P.7 is copy of Police intimation. Ex.P.8 is copy of Indemnity bond. Ex.P.9 is Outpatient record. Ex.P.10 and 13 are Lab reports. Ex.P.15 is X-rays. Ex.P.17 is OPD card and Ex.P.18 is X-ray. 
12. On going through the oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioner, it clearly appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 09.11.2021 at about 04.15 p.m, on Manduru - Gunduru Road, near BMTC Depot Turning Cross, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Ashok Leyland Tempo bearing No. KA-53-AA-0761 by its driver as alleged in the petition. Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative. 
Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/
4 13. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.608/2022 grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident. 
The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 30 years and was doing wood cutter labour work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and due to the accidental injuries, petitioner till today cannot attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning capacity and put to great financial hardship and became permanent disabled. 
14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth. 
However he has produced Ex.P.16 Aadhaar card. Eventhough the said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of cogent evidence with respect to date of birth of petitioner, the said document can be relied upon, according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 07.02.1991 and the alleged accident occurred on 09.11.2021. Therefore, it appears that as (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.608/2022 on the date of accident the age of petitioner is 30 years. Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 30 years as on the date of accident. As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.
15. With regard to avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal. Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m. Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/-.
16. According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained communited fracture of proximal tibia and fibula right leg and he assessed permanent physical disability of 44% of right lower limb which is 22% of whole body. However, considering (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.608/2022 the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%. Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
15,000/- x 12 x 17 x 10% = Rs.3,06,000/-.
17. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 Discharge summary, according to which the petitioner was admitted to East Point hospital,
Bengaluru, as inpatient for 10 days. During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition. 
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head. 
Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/
5 18. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and Ex.P.15 X-rays, Ex.P.17 OPD card and Ex.P.18 X-ray and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries. Accordingly with regard to grievous (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.608/2022 injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head. 
19. Loss of income during laid up period:- As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 10 days as inpatient. 
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months. Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
(Rs.15,000 x 2) under this head. 
20. Medical expenses:- As per Ex.P.14 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.79,677/-. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.79,677/- under the head of medical expenses. 
21. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.608/2022 Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness. 
22. Future medical expenses:- According to PW.2 doctor the petitioner needs further treatment for malunion of tibia and implant removal and in the cross-examination he stated that in their hospital for removal of implant cost nearly Rs.8,000/- to Rs.10,000/-. But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses. Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,000/- under this head. 
23. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:- 
 Sl. Head of Compensation Amount  No. in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 3,06,000-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00  3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges  4. Medical Expenses 79,677-00  5. Loss of future amenities in 30,000-00  life and unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid 30,000-00  up period  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.608/2022  7. Future medical expenses 10,000-00 Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/ 
6  Total 5,15,677-00 24. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,15,677/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
25. Regarding liability:- In this case, the respondent No.2 has taken several defences and in order to prove its defence and to disprove the case of the petitioner, the MRO of East Point hospital is examined as RW.1 and he has produced true copy of MLC extract as per Ex.R.1 and in the cross- examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that MLC was belongs to the petitioner and the injured was came to their hospital on the same day of accident. Hence, his evidence is also corroborated with the evidence of the petitioner. 
26. Further, the Legal Manager of respondent No.2 Insurance Company is examined as RW.2 and he has produced copy of Policy as per Ex.R.2 and during the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that they have not challenged the (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.608/2022 Charge sheet filed against the driver of the Tempo and also admits that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force and next day of the accident complaint was lodged and stated that he has not produced any document to show the rider was consuming alcohol, but he also admits that in the said document there is no mention of quantity of alcohol consumed by the petitioner. 
27. Further, on going through the oral and documentary evidence of the petitioner and respondents,
nothing is brought on records to show that the rider of the Motor Cycle/petitioner was consumed excess of alcohol in violation of provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act and caused accident. Moreover, on perusal of Ex.P.3 Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has not invoked provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act for drunk and drive by the rider. Therefore, the contention of respondent No.2 holds no water and not supported by the convincing evidence. Further, the respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 3 admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending Tempo. 
Further, on perusal of Ex.R.2 copy of Policy of the offending vehicle, wherein it is clearly mentioned (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.608/2022 that said policy is Goods Carriage policy and policy is valid from 24.07.2021 to 23.07.2022 and the alleged accident was occurred on 09.11.2021 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force. Hence,
respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners. 
However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.5,15,677/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-)
within two months from the date of this Judgment. Accordingly I answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative. 
28. Issue No.3: In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/
7 ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost. 
(SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.608/2022 The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,15,677/- (Rupees Five lakhs fifteen thousand six hundred and seventy seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization. 
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment. 
The petitioner is entitled to get release 75% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 25% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-. Draw award accordingly.

annotations.text: Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.608/2022 grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 30 years and was doing wood cutter labour work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and due to the accidental injuries, petitioner till today cannot attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning capacity and put to great financial hardship and became permanent disabled.
14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However he has produced Ex.P.16 Aadhaar card.

Eventhough the said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of cogent evidence with respect to date of birth of petitioner, the said document can be relied upon, according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 07.02.1991 and the alleged accident occurred on 09.11.2021.
Therefore, it appears that as (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.608/2022 on the date of accident the age of petitioner is 30 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 30 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.
15.

annotations.text: With regard to avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2021 to be taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,000/-.
16.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained communited fracture of proximal tibia and fibula right leg and he assessed permanent physical disability of 44% of right lower limb which is 22% of whole body.

However, considering (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.608/2022 the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 Discharge summary, according to which the petitioner was admitted to East Point hospital,
Bengaluru, as inpatient for 10 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

annotations.text: Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.5 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and Ex.P.15 X-rays, Ex.P.17 OPD card and Ex.P.18 X-ray and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.608/2022 injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
19. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 10 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
(Rs.15,000 x 2) under this head.
20. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.14 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.79,677/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.79,677/- under the head of medical expenses.

21. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.608/2022 Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
22. Future medical expenses:-

According to PW.2 doctor the petitioner needs further treatment for malunion of tibia and implant removal and in the cross-examination he stated that in their hospital for removal of implant cost nearly Rs.8,000/- to Rs.10,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,000/- under this head.
23. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges  4. Medical Expenses 79,677-00  5. Loss of future amenities in 30,000-00  life and unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid 30,000-00  up period  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.608/2022  7.
Future medical expenses 10,000-00 Nagaraju vs Sangamesh on 20 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82514421/

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,15,677/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
25.

Regarding liability:- In this case, the respondent No.2 has taken several defences and in order to prove its defence and to disprove the case of the petitioner, the MRO of East Point hospital is examined as RW.1 and he has produced true copy of MLC extract as per Ex.R.1 and in the cross- examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that MLC was belongs to the petitioner and the injured was came to their hospital on the same day of accident.
Hence, his evidence is also corroborated with the evidence of the petitioner.

26. Further, the Legal Manager of respondent No.2 Insurance Company is examined as RW.2 and he has produced copy of Policy as per Ex.R.2 and during the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that they have not challenged the (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.608/2022 Charge sheet filed against the driver of the Tempo and also admits that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force and next day of the accident complaint was lodged and stated that he has not produced any document to show the rider was consuming alcohol, but he also admits that in the said document there is no mention of quantity of alcohol consumed by the petitioner.

27. Further, on going through the oral and documentary evidence of the petitioner and respondents,
nothing is brought on records to show that the rider of the Motor Cycle/petitioner was consumed excess of alcohol in violation of provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act and caused accident.
Moreover, on perusal of Ex.P.3 Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has not invoked provisions of Sec.185 of M.V. Act for drunk and drive by the rider.
Therefore, the contention of respondent No.2 holds no water and not supported by the convincing evidence.
Further, the respondent No.2 in its written statement at para 3 admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending Tempo.

Further, on perusal of Ex.R.2 copy of Policy of the offending vehicle, wherein it is clearly mentioned (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.608/2022 that said policy is Goods Carriage policy and policy is valid from 24.07.2021 to 23.07.2022 and the alleged accident was occurred on 09.11.2021 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force.

Hence,
respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.5,15,677/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-)
within two months from the date of this Judgment.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
